title: Granular quotas and per-key/per-route analytics — UX sketches and backlog
content:
Purpose:

Capture lightweight UX sketches, interaction notes, and a groomed backlog for the per-key and per-route rate limiting / quota / usage analytics surfaces in Console. This doc is intentionally informal — sketches, microcopy, and acceptance criteria. Use as a reference for design/PM/engineering sync.

High-level goals:
- Give customers a single view to understand what each API key is doing (tokens, requests, routes) and why they might be throttled.
- Enable quick drilldown from broad usage to route-level detail and to offending requests.
- Provide actionable tooling: change quota windows, add burst allowances, set alerts, export CSV, and run a simulated throttle.
- Make per-key costs visible (unit cost / token * tokens = estimated spend) for customer ops and billing reconciliation.

Target personas:
- API consumer (developer/product engineer) who wants to debug a sudden spike.
- Platform owner (SRE/FinOps) who needs to see cost per team and apply caps.
- Support engineer who wants to triage a rate limit complaint.

Primary screens (wireframe notes):
1) Keys overview (list)
- Left column: key name, owner (team), active flag, creation date.
- Center: sparkline (7d requests) + current 1m RPS badge.
- Right: usage summary chips: tokens (24h), requests (24h), errors (24h), quota status (OK / Near / Breached).
- Row actions: View, Edit quotas, Simulate throttle, Export usage.
- Sorting: by tokens, by requests, by cost.
- Quick filter: team, region, key-type (hosted/dedicated/private).

Interaction notes: clicking row opens a slide-over (right rail) not a new page. Slide-over has the key detail and quick actions. This keeps context and allows rapid triage.

2) Key detail slide-over (summary pane)
- Header: key name + owner + last used timestamp + copy key token button (masked by default).
- Top row metrics (24h): Tokens, Requests, Avg latency, Error rate, Cost estimate. Each metric has a small (i) tooltip with calculation.
- Mini timeline: stacked area chart (tokens by route) with hover showing route breakdown. 1h/24h/7d toggle.
- Quota card: shows active quota windows (per-minute, per-hour, per-day), burst allowance, and next reset time. Primary CTA: Edit quotas. Secondary: Add burst.
- Live events feed: last 20 throttle events with route, timestamp, reason code, and sample request id. Click request id to open request inspector.

Microcopy / tooltips (draft):
- Quota status badge: OK (green): "Under configured quotas"; Near (yellow): "Approaching configured quota — consider raising or adding burst"; Throttled (red): "Requests were throttled — read events below".
- Cost estimate tooltip: "Estimated spend = tokens_used * model_unit_cost. Model unit cost is taken from active model profile; use billing page to adjust."

3) Route drilldown (from slide-over: "View route breakdown")
- Route list: route path, route alias, model used, tokens per request (p50/p95), requests per min, throttle rate%.
- Route detail page: toggle top: aggregated metrics over time window + waterfall chart showing which routes contribute to peak loads.
- Per-route quotas: allow override of key-level settings. Show inheritance indicators (inherited from key-level, overridden by route).

Interaction notes:
- Default drilldown loads a cached 1m resolution snapshot to avoid heavy queries; engineers can request full-res (5s) for the last hour if needed (button: "load live stream").

4) Request inspector (modal)
- Shows request headers (redacted), payload size, model, tokens consumed, KV cache hit ratio, start/end timestamps, latency breakdown per stage, and any throttle response.
- Offers link to replay request in staging (sandbox) — gated by role.

Metric definitions (for copy accuracy):
- Tokens: sum of input + output tokens computed by our tokenizer for the specific model.
- Requests: number of HTTP calls that hit inference surface. Retries are counted separately if received by our gateway.
- Throttle events: any response with HTTP 429 or internal rate-limit code (X-RateLimit-Reason).
- Cost estimate: tokens * model_unit_cost + request overhead. Model_unit_cost comes from model catalog metadata.

Backlog grooming (prioritized items):
- P0: Build Keys Overview table + slide-over with metrics and quota card. (INF-3241)
  - Acceptance: list loads in <300ms for 5k keys; slide-over open in <100ms for single key.
  - Tech notes: use pre-aggregated materialized views in clickhouse. Provide API: GET /console/keys?summary=true.
- P0: Implement per-route quotas UI and inheritance UI (CONS-112).
  - Acceptance: engineers can set an override on a route; UI shows clear"inherited" vs "overridden" state. Backend: persist routeQuotas on key+route pair.
- P1: Export CSV for key usage with filters (time window, routes).
- P1: Simulated throttle tool in UI (run on 5-minute window, returns list of requests that would be dropped).
- P2: Alert templating — prefilled thresholds and slack webhook quick-add for a key.
- P2: Cost breakdown per-model per-key and mapping to billing account.
- P3: Role-based permissioning in UI (who can edit quotas vs who can only view).

Edge cases and non-goals:
- We will not attempt full session replay (payloads with PII) in v1; request payloads should be redacted unless allowed.
- Per-tenant cross-key aggregation for shared-keys will be surfaced later (v-next).
- Not building a real-time streaming console for all keys in v1 — limited to the slide-over live stream toggles.

UX details and micro-interactions to capture in Figma:  
- Badge colors: green(#16A34A), yellow(#F59E0B), red(#EF4444). Ensure colorblind patterns (icons) accompany color.
- Small sparklines should be clickable for time-range zoom-in.
- Confirmation modal when increasing daily quotas over 20% for a key (to reduce accidental cost spikes).
- 'Simulate throttle' should run against a cached window and show a reason histogram (token-exhaustion vs per-route-limit).

Acceptance criteria (combined across features):
- Customers can find which key caused a spike in under 90s from the Keys Overview landing.
- Support can export the last 24h of throttle events for a given key in CSV format.
- Admins can set and persist per-route quota overrides and see immediate effect in the next aggregation window (~5m).

Open questions (to resolve in sync):
- How do we surface model switching in the route list? Should we show runbook for fallback variants? (cc: @Marcus Li)
- Quota window semantics: do we allow sliding windows or fixed boundaries? Initial plan: fixed windows (aligned to minute/hour/day) with an option for rolling windows v2.
- Cost estimates: where to read model_unit_cost for private deployments that set custom pricing? There needs to be mapping to billing config id. (action: coordinate with billing and private-deployments teams)

Implementation notes for backend (engineering pointers):
- Pre-aggregate tokens & requests per key+route per 1m in clickhouse. Keep 30d retention at 1m, 90d at 1h.
- Throttle events should be written to an events table with sample request id but with payload stripped. Keep last 10k events per key in fast store (redis stream) for slide-over feed.
- Authz: API endpoints must check role scoping: read-only for support; edit for admin; simulate gated to internal roles.

Design handoff checklist:
- [ ] Finalized Figma frames for Keys Overview, Key Slide-over, Route detail, Request inspector.
- [ ] Microcopy defined for badges, tooltips, confirmation modals.
- [ ] Acceptance criteria in Jira for P0/P1 items.
- [ ] Engineering API spec: GET /console/keys, GET /console/keys/{key}/routes, POST /console/keys/{key}/simulate

Next steps (this week):
- Monday: review with SRE and Billing (30m) — confirm cost calc and pre-agg windows. (Invite: @Diego Santos, @Nina Okoye)
- Tuesday: quick Figma sketch export and handoff to FE for prototype.
- Wednesday: grooming session with eng (1h) — break down INF-3241 into sub-tasks.

Notes-to-self (short):
- Keep the slide-over fast; avoid reloading entire page state.
- Expose a simple "why was I throttled" explainer at the top of the slide-over for non-technical users.
- Save ephemeral sample queries for support to reproduce throttles quickly.

Appendix: sample CSV columns (for export)
key_id, key_name, team, route, model, timestamp, tokens, requests, latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95, error_rate, throttle_reason, request_id

References:
- Slack thread: #console-product (rate-limits-dec2024) — contains early sketches and customer repros.
- Jira INF-3241 (Keys overview), CONS-112 (per-route overrides)
- PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/783 - initial table component work.

---
Document is intentionally lightweight. If you pick up implementation, update this doc with test-cases and a link to the Figma file.
